name: Copper Age
description: Turn your first copper into mechanical power and the beginnings of automation.

pages.text: $(bold)Welcome to the Copper Age$()$(br2)Your first Copper Ingot ends the Stone Age, but Copper is not just a stronger crafting material. This age is about learning to work metal, transmit rotational power, process ore mechanically, and gradually replace manual labor with machinery.$(br2)The intended Copper Age will be much longer than the Stone Age. Producing your first Bronze will eventually mark its end.

pages.title: Primitive Anvil
pages.text: The Primitive Anvil is your first metalworking station. It gives the Primitive Hammer a real job and turns raw ingots into machine components.

$(bold)1. Work your first Copper$()$(br2)Place a Copper Ingot onto the Primitive Anvil by right-clicking it. Strike the ingot four times with the Primitive Hammer to flatten it into a $(item)Copper Plate$().$(br2)Use an empty hand to take the finished item back.$(br2)Copper Plates are the first manufactured Copper Age component and are accepted through the standard $(thing)forge:plates/copper$() tag.

$(bold)2. Mechanical Power$()$(br2)Copper lets you reinforce wooden mechanical components. Shafts carry rotation along an axis, while gears transfer rotation between parallel axes.$(br2)The current wooden system has Medium and Large gears. Gear size affects both speed and torque: changing gear size changes the ratio instead of creating free power.

pages.title: Shafts & Medium Gears
pages.text: Shafts form the backbone of a mechanical line. Medium gears are the smaller 8-tooth gear.

pages.title: Large Gears & Handle
pages.text: The handled Large Gear is your first power source. Right-click it to crank the network for a limited time. Ordinary gears no longer become free power sources from Redstone.

$(bold)Manual Mechanical Era$()$(br2)At the start of the Copper Age, every mechanical machine is intended to depend on human input. The handled gear produces rotation for a short period, so early workshops must be cranked by hand.$(br2)This inconvenience is intentional: obtaining continuous mechanical power later should feel like a major technological milestone.

$(bold)Next: Mechanical Grinder$()$(br2)The first machine planned for this network is the Mechanical Grinder. It will turn ore processing from a purely manual smelting chain into a mechanical one and improve material yield.$(br2)This part of the Copper Age is still under construction.

$(bold)Planned Copper Age milestones$()$(br2)After manual mechanical processing, the age is planned to expand into continuous rotational power, improved Copper metallurgy, and basic item logistics.$(br2)The goal is for the player to finish Copper Age with a small functioning mechanical workshop rather than simply crafting a list of machines.

$(bold)The road to Bronze$()$(br2)Cassiterite and Tin will form the final Copper Age challenge. Tin processing is intended to depend on the mechanical infrastructure learned during this age.$(br2)Combining processed Tin with Copper to produce the first Bronze will eventually mark the transition into the Bronze Age.
